Parent: WL-0MKRJK13H1VCHLPZ - Epic: Add bd-equivalent workflow commands

Add first-class dependency tracking (blocks/blockedBy + typed edges like discovered-from) and use it to power `worklog ready` (unblocked work detection).

Implementation:
- Persist dependency edges between items (direction + type).
- CLI/API: `worklog dep add|rm|list` with edge types and output formats.
- `worklog ready` returns items with no unresolved blocking deps (optionally filtered by status/assignee/tags).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can add/remove/list dependencies and see them on items.
- `worklog ready` excludes items blocked by open dependencies and includes unblocked items.
- Supports at least `blocks` and `discovered-from` edge types.
data.title: Feature: Dependency tracking + ready

data.description:
Add `worklog close` to mirror `bd close`, supporting single and multiple ids and a stored close reason.

Implementation:
- CLI: `worklog close <id...> [--reason "..."]`.
- Store close reason on the item (field) or as an immutable comment/event.
- Set status to `completed` and update timestamps consistently.

Acceptance criteria:
- Closing one or many ids marks each item `completed`.
- `--reason` is persisted and visible via `wl show`.
- Command reports per-id success/failure and returns non-zero if any close fails.
data.title: Feature: worklog close (single + multi)

Add “plan/insights/diff” style commands (or API endpoints) analogous to bv robot outputs: critical path, cycles, and “what changed since ref/date”.

Add branch-per-item support: `worklog branch <id>` creates/switches to a branch named with the id (optionally records branch on item).

Add “landing the plane” automation: `worklog land` runs configurable quality gates, ensures worklog/issue data sync, and verifies git push success.

Implementation:

data.description: Feature: Full-text search (SQLite FTS) — WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 Brief summary - Add an FTS5-backed full-text search index and a `worklog search` CLI so contributors can run fast, ranked queries (title, description, comments, tags) with immediate index visibility after writes. Problem statement - Developers and maintainers need fast, relevant full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags) so they can find and triage issues reliably at scale. Current listing and filtering are limited and do not support relevance ranking, snippets, or fast text queries. Users - Repository contributors and maintainers who search work items to triage, plan, and debug. Example user stories: - As a contributor, I want to run `worklog search "database corruption"` and see the most relevant items (with snippets) so I can find prior discussions quickly. - As a release engineer, I want to filter search results by `--status open --tags cli` and export JSON for automation so I can programmatically build reports. - As a maintainer, I want the search index to reflect writes immediately so newly created/updated items are discoverable in the next command. Chosen approach (capture fidelity) - SQLite FTS5 is the target engine (user confirmed). Index all text fields plus tags (title, description, comments, tags, other text fields). CLI defaults: human-friendly output with snippets and filters; `--json` for machine consumption. Success criteria - Search returns ranked, relevant results for common queries (top-10 relevance) with snippet highlights matching query terms. - Index updates synchronously on write: create/update/delete operations are visible to subsequent searches within 1 second. - CLI usability: `worklog search ` supports `--status`, `--parent`, `--tags`, `--json`, `--limit` and returns human-friendly output by default; `--json` returns structured results. - Performance: median query latency <100ms on datasets up to ~5,000 items in CI/dev environment; include a small benchmark job in CI. - Tests & CI: unit tests for indexing/querying, integration fixtures covering index correctness and consistency across create/update/delete, and a perf benchmark. Constraints - Requires SQLite with FTS5 enabled; the CLI must detect and fail fast with a clear message if FTS5 is unavailable. - Keep index consistent with the canonical store (SQLite DB or `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` import flow). Prefer DB-backed storage and transactional updates. - Implement synchronous updates with minimal write latency (FTS virtual table + triggers or application-managed transactions that update FTS in the same transaction). Existing state & traceability - Work item: WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 (Feature: Full-text search). - Parent epic: WL-0MKRJK13H1VCHLPZ — Epic: Add bd-equivalent workflow commands. - Related infra: WL-0MKRRZ2DN0898F / WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP — Persist Worklog DB across executions; these inform DB choice/lifecycle. - Source data: `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — use for initial backfill and test fixtures. - Docs: update `CLI.md` with `worklog search` usage and examples. Desired change (high level) - Add FTS5 virtual table `worklog_fts` that indexes title, description, comment bodies, tags and other text fields; include per-document metadata (work item id, status, parentId) to support filtering and ranking. - Keep index in sync synchronously on write via triggers or application-managed transactions; provide `--rebuild-index` admin flag to backfill or rebuild. - Implement `worklog search` supporting: phrase queries, prefix search, bm25 ranking, snippet extraction, filters `--status/--parent/--tags`, `--limit`, and `--json` output. - Provide migration/bootstrap: create FTS table on first run and backfill from `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` or current DB. Example SQL (developer handoff) ``` -- Create a simple FTS5 table tying back to the canonical items table CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS worklog_fts USING fts5( title, description, comments, tags, itemId UNINDEXED, status UNINDEXED, parentId UNINDEXED, tokenize = 'porter' ); -- Example ranked query with snippet SELECT itemId, bm25(worklog_fts) AS rank, snippet(worklog_fts, '', '', '...', -1, 64) AS snippet FROM worklog_fts WHERE worklog_fts MATCH '"database corruption" OR database*' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10; ``` Related work (links/ids) - WL-0MKRPG61W1NKGY78 — this item. - WL-0MKRJK13H1VCHLPZ — parent epic. - WL-0MKRRZ2DN0898F / WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP — DB persistence work (relevant). - `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — backfill and fixtures. - `CLI.md` — update after implementation. Risks & mitigations - FTS5 unavailable in some SQLite builds — Mitigation: detect early, emit a clear error message and document runtime requirements; create a follow-up fallback task if adoption is required. - Noisy/irrelevant results — Mitigation: tune tokenization, add field weighting, provide examples in docs, and expose `--limit` and filter flags for deterministic results. - Index corruption or schema drift during upgrades — Mitigation: provide `--rebuild-index`, export/backups before migration, and include migration scripts in the PR. - Write latency on very large datasets — Mitigation: measure with CI benchmark; keep transactional updates fast; evaluate async updates as follow-up if necessary. Polish & handoff - Update `CLI.md` with usage examples and the SQL snippet above. Include a short dev guide in the PR describing bootstrap steps, `--rebuild-index`, and how to run the perf benchmark. - Final one-line headline for work item body: "FTS5-backed full-text search + `worklog search` CLI: fast, ranked queries over title, description, comments and tags with synchronous indexing." Suggested next steps (conservative) 1) Merge this intake draft into the work item description (after your approval). 2) Create a small spike branch: add FTS5 table + backfill script + prototype `worklog search --json` and run local perf tests. 3) If FTS5 is absent in some environments, open a follow-up work item to add an application-level fallback.
data.title: Full-text search

data.description:
# Worklog doctor intake brief (WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6)

## Problem statement
Worklog lacks a reliable, non-destructive diagnostics command to evaluate the integrity and consistency of worklog data during regular use. We need `worklog doctor` to report integrity issues, apply safe workflow-alignment fixes, and interactively handle non-safe fixes without tying results to build/CI failure semantics.

## Users
- Maintainers and SREs who need to validate worklog data health during routine operations.
- Developers and agents who need clear diagnostics and guided remediation when issues are found.

### Example user stories
- As a maintainer, I want `worklog doctor` to summarize integrity problems and guide fixes so the worklog remains consistent during daily use.
- As a developer, I want `worklog doctor --fix` to apply safe workflow-alignment fixes automatically and prompt me on non-safe changes.

## Success criteria
- `worklog doctor` reports integrity findings for graph integrity and status/stage validation.
- Human output is an informative summary; `--json` outputs a single array of detailed findings.
- `--fix` applies safe fixes automatically and prompts interactively for non-safe fixes.
- Safe fixes are limited to workflow-alignment changes; non-safe fixes are never applied without user confirmation.
- The command is usable during regular operations and does not imply CI/build failure behavior.

## Suggested next step
Proceed to implementation planning for `worklog doctor` with `--fix` support, aligning graph integrity and status/stage validation checks to the documented rules and data stores.

## Constraints
- No `--fail-on` or build/CI failure semantics.
- No severity labels on findings.
- Fixing is interactive for non-safe changes.
- Operate on the canonical worklog datastore (DB) and existing JSONL exports.

## Existing state
- Work items and dependency edges are persisted in `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and the SQLite DB.
- Status/stage rules and known validation gaps are documented in `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md`.

## Desired change
- Implement `worklog doctor [--json] [--fix]`.
- Detect graph integrity issues (cycles, missing parents, dangling dependency edges, orphaned non-epic items, malformed/duplicate ids if format rules exist).
- Detect status/stage values that violate config-driven rules.
- Produce an informative human summary by default; `--json` emits a single array of detailed findings.
- When `--fix` is enabled:
  - Apply safe fixes automatically (workflow-alignment changes).
  - Prompt interactively for non-safe fixes (anything not easily reversible).
  - Report any declined non-safe fixes as remaining findings.

## Related work
- Doctor: detect missing dep references (WL-0ML4PH4EQ1XODFM0) — child item for dangling dependency checks.
- Doctor: validate status/stage values from config (WL-0MLE6WJUY0C5RRVX) — child item for status/stage validation.
- Add wl dep command (WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US) — dependency edges and semantics.
data.title: wl doctor

The goal is for us to be able to keep issues in sync across multiple instances of worklog. We currently have the ability to export and import, but there is currently no version control features.

When we do a git pull the latest jsonl file will be retrieved but it currently will not be imported into the database. Furthermore, there may be convlicts that need to be resolved.

Create a sync command that will pull the latest file from git (only the jsonl file), merge the content - including resolving conflicts (use the updatedAt to indicate the most recent data that should take precendence). Export the data and push the latest back to git.

Generate the best possible algorithm to make this happen, do not feel constrained by the detail of my request here, the goal is to ensure that when the sync command is run the local database has all the latest remote updates and the current local updates.

data.description:
Problem
- Worklog currently uses a Map-backed in-memory database (src/database.ts) and relies on importing/exporting .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl per CLI invocation (src/cli.ts) and at API server startup (src/index.ts).
- There is no persistent database process/state that survives between separate CLI runs, and the “source of truth”/refresh behavior is ad-hoc.
- We want a real persistent DB (on disk) so the database state exists independently of a single process, and a clear refresh rule: if the local JSONL file is newer than what the DB has, reload/refresh the DB from JSONL.
Goal
- Replace the “in-memory Map only” approach with a disk-backed database that persists between command executions.
- Ensure the DB automatically refreshes from .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl when that file is newer than the DB’s current state.
Proposed behavior
- On CLI start and API server start:
  - Open/connect to the persistent DB stored on disk (location configurable; default under .worklog/).
  - Determine staleness:
    - Compare JSONL mtime vs DB “last imported from JSONL” timestamp (or DB file mtime if that’s the chosen proxy).
  - If JSONL is newer:
    - Re-import from JSONL into the DB (rebuild items/comments).
    - Update DB metadata to record the import time + source file path + JSONL mtime/hash (so future comparisons are reliable).
- On writes (create/update/delete/comment ops):
  - Persist to DB immediately.
  - Decide and document the new “source of truth” model:
    - Option A: DB is source of truth; JSONL is an export artifact (write JSONL on demand or on a schedule).
    - Option B: Keep writing JSONL for Git workflows, but DB remains authoritative for runtime and only refreshes from JSONL when JSONL is newer (e.g., after a git pull).
Scope / tasks
- Add a persistent DB implementation (likely SQLite) and a small DB metadata table, e.g.:
  - meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT) with keys like lastJsonlImportMtimeMs, lastJsonlImportAt, schemaVersion.
- Refactor database layer:
  - Introduce an interface (e.g. WorklogStore) implemented by the new persistent DB.
  - Keep the current Map DB as a fallback/dev option if desired, but default to persistent.
- Update CLI (src/cli.ts):
  - Replace loadData()/saveData() logic with “open DB; maybe refresh from JSONL; operate on DB; optionally export JSONL”.
  - Ensure multi-project prefix behavior still works.
- Update API server startup (src/index.ts):
  - Same refresh logic on boot.
- Refresh logic details:
  - Use fs.statSync(jsonlPath).mtimeMs (or async equivalent).
  - Compare against stored DB metadata value; if JSONL missing, do nothing.
  - If DB is empty/uninitialized and JSONL exists, import.
- Add migration/versioning:
  - DB schema version stored in metadata; handle upgrades safely.
- Tests / acceptance checks
  - Running worklog create then a separate worklog list shows the created item without relying on in-process state.
  - If .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is modified externally (simulate git pull), the next CLI/API startup refreshes DB and reflects the updated data.
  - If DB has newer data than JSONL, it does not overwrite DB (unless explicitly commanded); behavior is documented.
Acceptance criteria
- DB persists across separate CLI executions (verified by creating an item, exiting, re-running list/show).
- On startup (CLI + API), if .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is newer than DB state, DB is refreshed from JSONL automatically.
- No data loss when switching from current JSONL-only workflow: existing .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is imported into the new DB on first run.
- Clear documented “source of truth” and when JSONL is written/updated.
Notes / implementation preference
- SQLite is a good default (single file on disk, easy distribution, supports concurrency better than ad-hoc JSON).
- Keep .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl for Git-friendly sharing, but treat it as an import/export boundary rather than the primary store.
data.title: Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer

data.description:
Users should be able to download a release artifact, extract it, place it on their PATH, and run worklog without installing Node or running npm install. We’ll implement a per-platform “folder distribution” that bundles:
- a small worklog launcher (or worklog.exe)
- a Node.js runtime
- the compiled Worklog CLI (dist/)
- runtime dependencies, including the native better-sqlite3 addon for that platform
This is explicitly not a single-file executable; it’s a self-contained directory that can be put on PATH.
Goals
- worklog runs on a clean machine with no Node/npm installed.
- Distributions are produced for at least: linux-x64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win-x64 (expand as needed).
- Release artifact layout is stable and documented.
- CLI behavior is unchanged (same commands/options/output).
Non-goals
- Single-file executable.
- Replacing better-sqlite3.
- Building from source on user machines.
Implementation plan
1) Choose packaging approach (recommended)
- Bundle Node runtime + app into a folder:
  - node (or node.exe)
  - worklog launcher script/binary that executes the bundled node:
    - linux/macos: ./node ./dist/cli.js "$@"
    - windows: worklog.cmd or worklog.exe shim calling node.exe dist\cli.js %*
  - dist/ output from tsc
  - node_modules/ containing production deps (incl. better-sqlite3 compiled binary)
2) Add packaging scripts
- Add npm run build (already exists) + new scripts such as:
  - npm run dist:prep to create a clean staging directory
  - npm run dist:bundle to copy dist/, package.json, and install production deps into staging
  - npm run dist:node:<platform> to download/extract the correct Node runtime into staging (or use a build action to fetch it)
  - npm run dist:archive to produce .tar.gz / .zip per platform
- Ensure we install prod-only deps into staging (no devDependencies).
3) Handle native module compatibility (better-sqlite3)
- Build artifacts must be produced on each target OS/arch (or use CI runners per platform) so better-sqlite3’s .node binary matches the target.
- Verify that the bundled node version matches the ABI expected by the built better-sqlite3 binary (i.e., build/install using the same Node major version you bundle).
4) Entrypoint and pathing
- Ensure the CLI entry works when executed from anywhere:
  - Use process.execPath / import.meta.url-relative paths so it finds dist/ and bundled resources regardless of current working directory.
- Confirm that .worklog/ data paths remain in the current project directory (unchanged).
5) Versioning and update UX
- Add worklog --version (already) and optionally a worklog version --json output for tooling (optional).
- Document upgrade procedure: replace the folder on PATH with a newer version.
6) CI build + GitHub releases
- Add GitHub Actions workflow:
  - Matrix: ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest (and macos for both x64/arm64 as appropriate)
  - Steps: checkout, install, build, stage folder, run smoke tests, archive, upload artifacts
  - On tag push: create GitHub Release and attach artifacts
7) Smoke tests (required)
- On each platform artifact in CI:
  - Extract artifact
  - Run ./worklog --help
  - Run ./worklog --version
  - Optionally run a minimal command that doesn’t require repo init (e.g., worklog status should error cleanly) to confirm runtime works.
8) Documentation
- Update README.md with:
  - Download links / artifact names
  - Install instructions per OS (PATH update examples)
  - Notes about per-platform downloads
  - Troubleshooting: macOS Gatekeeper/quarantine, Linux executable bit, Windows SmartScreen
Acceptance criteria
- A user can:
  - download the correct artifact for their OS/arch
  - extract it
  - add the extracted directory to PATH
  - run worklog --help successfully with no Node/npm installed
- CI produces and uploads artifacts for the supported platforms on every release tag.
- Artifacts include better-sqlite3 correctly (no missing native module errors).
Notes / risks
- macOS: may require signing/notarization for best UX; at minimum document Gatekeeper prompts.
- Windows: consider providing both worklog.cmd shim and (optional) an .exe shim.
- Size: bundling Node increases artifact size; this is expected for “no Node required”.
data.title: Ship Standalone “Folder Binary” Distribution (No npm install) for Worklog CLI

As work is undertaken we will need to record comments against work items. Each work item will have 0..n comments, each comment will have a single work item parent.

Comments will need the following fields:

- author - the name of the author of the comment (freeform string)
- comment - the text of the comment, in markdown format
- createdAt - the time the comment was created
- references - an array of references in the form of work item IDs, relative filepaths from the root of the current project, or URLs

data.description:
We want the Worklog CLI (dist/cli.js, implemented in src/cli.ts) to support a pluggable command architecture where new commands can be added by dropping a compiled ESM plugin file (.js / .mjs) into a known directory, with no Worklog rebuild required. On the next CLI invocation, the new command should appear automatically.
This issue also migrates all existing built-in commands out of src/cli.ts into external command modules (shipped with the package), using the same plugin interface, and fully documents the feature.
Goals
- Pluggable commands discovered at runtime (from disk) and registered into commander.
- All existing commands ported to external command modules (no giant monolith src/cli.ts).
- Clear docs: how to write, build, install, and troubleshoot plugins.
Non-goals
- Loading TypeScript plugins directly.
- Hot-reloading commands within a single long-running CLI session (CLI restart is sufficient).
Proposed design
- Define a plugin contract:
  - Each plugin is an ESM module exporting default as register(ctx): void (or named register).
  - register receives:
    - program: Command (commander instance)
    - ctx shared utilities (output helpers, config/db accessors, version, paths)
- Command module shape (example):
  - export default function register({ program, ctx }) { program.command('foo')... }
- Built-in commands:
  - Move each top-level command (and subcommand groups like comment) into its own module under src/commands/.
  - src/cli.ts becomes a thin bootstrap:
    - create program, global options, shared ctx
    - register built-in commands by importing ./commands/*.js
    - load external plugins from plugin dir and register them
- External plugin discovery:
  - Default plugin directory: .worklog/plugins/ (within the current repo/workdir).
  - Optional override: WORKLOG_PLUGIN_DIR env var and/or config key (documented).
  - Load order:
    - Built-ins first
    - Then external plugins in deterministic order (e.g., lexicographic by filename)
  - Only load files matching *.mjs / *.js (ignore .d.ts, maps, etc.)
  - Use dynamic import() with pathToFileURL() to load ESM from absolute paths.
- Name collisions:
  - If a plugin registers a command name that already exists, fail fast with a clear error (or optionally “plugin wins” via a flag; pick one and document).
- Observability:
  - Add worklog plugins command to list discovered plugins, load status, and any errors (also useful for debugging CI installs).
  - Add --verbose (or reuse an existing pattern) to print plugin load diagnostics.
Documentation requirements
- Add a new docs section (README or dedicated doc) covering:
  - Plugin directory, supported file extensions, load timing (next invocation)
  - Plugin API contract and examples
  - How to author a plugin in a separate repo/package:
    - compile to ESM ("type":"module", output .mjs or .js)
    - place built artifact into .worklog/plugins/
  - Security model (“plugins execute arbitrary code; only use trusted plugins”)
  - Troubleshooting: module resolution, ESM/CJS pitfalls, stack traces, worklog plugins
Migration scope (port all existing commands)
- Break out everything currently defined in src/cli.ts:
  - init, status, create, list, show, update, delete, export, import, next, sync
  - comment command group and its subcommands
- Preserve behavior:
  - Options, defaults, JSON output mode, error exit codes, config/db behaviors, sync behavior
  - Help text (--help) remains coherent and complete
Implementation tasks
- Create src/commands/ modules:
  - One module per command (or per command group), exporting a register(...) function
- Create shared CLI context/util module:
  - output helpers, requireInitialized, db factory, config access, dataPath, constants
- Add plugin loader:
  - Resolve plugin directory, discover files, dynamic import, call register
  - Collect and surface load errors
- Add plugins command for introspection
- Update build output wiring so built-in command modules compile to dist/commands/*
- Update README/docs and add at least one end-to-end plugin example
Testing / verification
- Unit tests for:
  - plugin discovery filtering and deterministic ordering
  - plugin load error handling
  - collision handling
- Integration-ish tests (vitest spawning node) for:
  - dropping a plugin file into a temp plugin dir and verifying --help includes the new command
  - worklog plugins reporting
- Ensure npm pack / global install style still works (bin points to dist/cli.js)
Acceptance criteria
- Dropping a compiled ESM plugin file into .worklog/plugins/ makes its command appear on next worklog --help run, without rebuilding Worklog.
- All existing commands are implemented as external command modules (no large command definitions left in src/cli.ts besides bootstrap + shared wiring).
- Documentation added and accurate; includes a minimal plugin example and troubleshooting.
- Tests cover plugin discovery and basic loading behavior.
Notes / risks
- ESM-only environment: plugins must be ESM; document clearly.
- Running arbitrary local code: document security implications; consider an opt-out config/env to disable plugin loading if needed.
data.title: Add Pluggable CLI Command System (JS plugins), migrate built-in commands, and document

data.description:
We need a `next` command that will evaluate the state of the database and suggest the next item that should be worked on. Initially this will be a simplistic algorithm as follows:

- Find in progress items.
- If there are none currently in progress find the item that is highest priority and oldest (created first).
- If there are in progress items walk down the tree of the highest priority / oldest item until you find all the leaf nodes that are not in progress
- Select the leaf node that is highest priority and oldest

When the result is presented, if we are not using --json then the user should offered the opportunity to copy the ID into the clipboard.

It should be possible to filter the results by --assignee.

It should be possible to provide a search term that will fuzzy match against title, description and comments (any item without the search term in one of these places will not be considered).

Note that later iterations will use more complex algorithms for identifying the next item.

data.description:
The current comment command structure is

```
# Create a comment on a work item
npm run cli -- comment-create WI-1 -a "John Doe" -c "This is a comment with **markdown**" -r "WI-2,src/api.ts,https://example.com"

# List comments for a work item
npm run cli -- comment-list WI-1

# Show a specific comment
npm run cli -- comment-show WI-C1

# Update a comment
npm run cli -- comment-update WI-C1 -c "Updated comment text"

# Delete a comment
npm run cli -- comment-delete WI-C1
```

Chang this to use sub commands as shown below:

```
# Create a comment on a work item
npm run cli -- comment create WI-1 -a "John Doe" -c "This is a comment with **markdown**" -r "WI-2,src/api.ts,https://example.com"

# List comments for a work item
npm run cli -- comment list WI-1

# Show a specific comment
npm run cli -- comment show WI-C1

# Update a comment
npm run cli -- comment update WI-C1 -c "Updated comment text"

# Delete a comment
npm run cli -- comment delete WI-C1
```

data.description:
Users should be able to download a release artifact, extract it, place it on their PATH, and run worklog without installing Node or running npm install. We’ll implement a per-platform “folder distribution” that bundles:
- a small worklog launcher (or worklog.exe)
- a Node.js runtime
- the compiled Worklog CLI (dist/)
- runtime dependencies, including the native better-sqlite3 addon for that platform
This is explicitly not a single-file executable; it’s a self-contained directory that can be put on PATH.
Goals
- worklog runs on a clean machine with no Node/npm installed.
- Distributions are produced for at least: linux-x64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win-x64 (expand as needed).
- Release artifact layout is stable and documented.
- CLI behavior is unchanged (same commands/options/output).
Non-goals
- Single-file executable.
- Replacing better-sqlite3.
- Building from source on user machines.
Implementation plan
1) Choose packaging approach (recommended)
- Bundle Node runtime + app into a folder:
  - node (or node.exe)
  - worklog launcher script/binary that executes the bundled node:
    - linux/macos: ./node ./dist/cli.js "$@"
    - windows: worklog.cmd or worklog.exe shim calling node.exe dist\cli.js %*
  - dist/ output from tsc
  - node_modules/ containing production deps (incl. better-sqlite3 compiled binary)
2) Add packaging scripts
- Add npm run build (already exists) + new scripts such as:
  - npm run dist:prep to create a clean staging directory
  - npm run dist:bundle to copy dist/, package.json, and install production deps into staging
  - npm run dist:node:<platform> to download/extract the correct Node runtime into staging (or use a build action to fetch it)
  - npm run dist:archive to produce .tar.gz / .zip per platform
- Ensure we install prod-only deps into staging (no devDependencies).
3) Handle native module compatibility (better-sqlite3)
- Build artifacts must be produced on each target OS/arch (or use CI runners per platform) so better-sqlite3’s .node binary matches the target.
- Verify that the bundled node version matches the ABI expected by the built better-sqlite3 binary (i.e., build/install using the same Node major version you bundle).
4) Entrypoint and pathing
- Ensure the CLI entry works when executed from anywhere:
  - Use process.execPath / import.meta.url-relative paths so it finds dist/ and bundled resources regardless of current working directory.
- Confirm that .worklog/ data paths remain in the current project directory (unchanged).
5) Versioning and update UX
- Add worklog --version (already) and optionally a worklog version --json output for tooling (optional).
- Document upgrade procedure: replace the folder on PATH with a newer version.
6) CI build + GitHub releases
- Add GitHub Actions workflow:
  - Matrix: ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest (and macos for both x64/arm64 as appropriate)
  - Steps: checkout, install, build, stage folder, run smoke tests, archive, upload artifacts
  - On tag push: create GitHub Release and attach artifacts
7) Smoke tests (required)
- On each platform artifact in CI:
  - Extract artifact
  - Run ./worklog --help
  - Run ./worklog --version
  - Optionally run a minimal command that doesn’t require repo init (e.g., worklog status should error cleanly) to confirm runtime works.
8) Documentation
- Update README.md with:
  - Download links / artifact names
  - Install instructions per OS (PATH update examples)
  - Notes about per-platform downloads
  - Troubleshooting: macOS Gatekeeper/quarantine, Linux executable bit, Windows SmartScreen
Acceptance criteria
- A user can:
  - download the correct artifact for their OS/arch
  - extract it
  - add the extracted directory to PATH
  - run worklog --help successfully with no Node/npm installed
- CI produces and uploads artifacts for the supported platforms on every release tag.
- Artifacts include better-sqlite3 correctly (no missing native module errors).
Notes / risks
- macOS: may require signing/notarization for best UX; at minimum document Gatekeeper prompts.
- Windows: consider providing both worklog.cmd shim and (optional) an .exe shim.
- Size: bundling Node increases artifact size; this is expected for “no Node required”.

On the next CLI invocation, the new command should appear automatically.
This issue also migrates all existing built-in commands out of src/cli.ts into external command modules (shipped with the package), using the same plugin interface, and fully documents the feature.
Goals
- Pluggable commands discovered at runtime (from disk) and registered into commander.
- All existing commands ported to external command modules (no giant monolith src/cli.ts).
- Clear docs: how to write, build, install, and troubleshoot plugins.
Non-goals
- Loading TypeScript plugins directly.
- Hot-reloading commands within a single long-running CLI session (CLI restart is sufficient).
Proposed design
- Define a plugin contract:
  - Each plugin is an ESM module exporting default as register(ctx): void (or named register).
  - register receives:
    - program: Command (commander instance)
    - ctx shared utilities (output helpers, config/db accessors, version, paths)
- Command module shape (example):
  - export default function register({ program, ctx }) { program.command('foo')... }
- Built-in commands:
  - Move each top-level command (and subcommand groups like comment) into its own module under src/commands/.
  - src/cli.ts becomes a thin bootstrap:
    - create program, global options, shared ctx
    - register built-in commands by importing ./commands/*.js
    - load external plugins from plugin dir and register them
- External plugin discovery:
  - Default plugin directory: .worklog/plugins/ (within the current repo/workdir).
  - Optional override: WORKLOG_PLUGIN_DIR env var and/or config key (documented).
  - Load order:
    - Built-ins first
    - Then external plugins in deterministic order (e.g., lexicographic by filename)
  - Only load files matching *.mjs / *.js (ignore .d.ts, maps, etc.)
  - Use dynamic import() with pathToFileURL() to load ESM from absolute paths.
- Name collisions:
  - If a plugin registers a command name that already exists, fail fast with a clear error (or optionally “plugin wins” via a flag; pick one and document).
- Observability:
  - Add worklog plugins command to list discovered plugins, load status, and any errors (also useful for debugging CI installs).
  - Add --verbose (or reuse an existing pattern) to print plugin load diagnostics.
Documentation requirements
- Add a new docs section (README or dedicated doc) covering:
  - Plugin directory, supported file extensions, load timing (next invocation)
  - Plugin API contract and examples
  - How to author a plugin in a separate repo/package:
    - compile to ESM ("type":"module", output .mjs or .js)
    - place built artifact into .worklog/plugins/
  - Security model (“plugins execute arbitrary code; only use trusted plugins”)
  - Troubleshooting: module resolution, ESM/CJS pitfalls, stack traces, worklog plugins
Migration scope (port all existing commands)
- Break out everything currently defined in src/cli.ts:
  - init, status, create, list, show, update, delete, export, import, next, sync
  - comment command group and its subcommands
- Preserve behavior:
  - Options, defaults, JSON output mode, error exit codes, config/db behaviors, sync behavior
  - Help text (--help) remains coherent and complete
Implementation tasks
- Create src/commands/ modules:
  - One module per command (or per command group), exporting a register(...) function
- Create shared CLI context/util module:
  - output helpers, requireInitialized, db factory, config access, dataPath, constants
- Add plugin loader:
  - Resolve plugin directory, discover files, dynamic import, call register
  - Collect and surface load errors
- Add plugins command for introspection
- Update build output wiring so built-in command modules compile to dist/commands/*
- Update README/docs and add at least one end-to-end plugin example
Testing / verification
- Unit tests for:
  - plugin discovery filtering and deterministic ordering
  - plugin load error handling
  - collision handling
- Integration-ish tests (vitest spawning node) for:
  - dropping a plugin file into a temp plugin dir and verifying --help includes the new command
  - worklog plugins reporting
- Ensure npm pack / global install style still works (bin points to dist/cli.js)
Acceptance criteria
- Dropping a compiled ESM plugin file into .worklog/plugins/ makes its command appear on next worklog --help run, without rebuilding Worklog.
- All existing commands are implemented as external command modules (no large command definitions left in src/cli.ts besides bootstrap + shared wiring).
- Documentation added and accurate; includes a minimal plugin example and troubleshooting.
- Tests cover plugin discovery and basic loading behavior.
Notes / risks
- ESM-only environment: plugins must be ESM; document clearly.
- Running arbitrary local code: document security implications; consider an opt-out config/env to disable plugin loading if needed.

data.description:
Problem
- Worklog currently uses a Map-backed in-memory database (src/database.ts) and relies on importing/exporting .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl per CLI invocation (src/cli.ts) and at API server startup (src/index.ts).
- There is no persistent database process/state that survives between separate CLI runs, and the “source of truth”/refresh behavior is ad-hoc.
- We want a real persistent DB (on disk) so the database state exists independently of a single process, and a clear refresh rule: if the local JSONL file is newer than what the DB has, reload/refresh the DB from JSONL.
Goal
- Replace the “in-memory Map only” approach with a disk-backed database that persists between command executions.
- Ensure the DB automatically refreshes from .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl when that file is newer than the DB’s current state.
Proposed behavior
- On CLI start and API server start:
  - Open/connect to the persistent DB stored on disk (location configurable; default under .worklog/).
  - Determine staleness:
    - Compare JSONL mtime vs DB “last imported from JSONL” timestamp (or DB file mtime if that’s the chosen proxy).
  - If JSONL is newer:
    - Re-import from JSONL into the DB (rebuild items/comments).
    - Update DB metadata to record the import time + source file path + JSONL mtime/hash (so future comparisons are reliable).
- On writes (create/update/delete/comment ops):
  - Persist to DB immediately.
  - Decide and document the new “source of truth” model:
    - Option A: DB is source of truth; JSONL is an export artifact (write JSONL on demand or on a schedule).
    - Option B: Keep writing JSONL for Git workflows, but DB remains authoritative for runtime and only refreshes from JSONL when JSONL is newer (e.g., after a git pull).
Scope / tasks
- Add a persistent DB implementation (likely SQLite) and a small DB metadata table, e.g.:
  - meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT) with keys like lastJsonlImportMtimeMs, lastJsonlImportAt, schemaVersion.
- Refactor database layer:
  - Introduce an interface (e.g. WorklogStore) implemented by the new persistent DB.
  - Keep the current Map DB as a fallback/dev option if desired, but default to persistent.
- Update CLI (src/cli.ts):
  - Replace loadData()/saveData() logic with “open DB; maybe refresh from JSONL; operate on DB; optionally export JSONL”.
  - Ensure multi-project prefix behavior still works.
- Update API server startup (src/index.ts):
  - Same refresh logic on boot.
- Refresh logic details:
  - Use fs.statSync(jsonlPath).mtimeMs (or async equivalent).
  - Compare against stored DB metadata value; if JSONL missing, do nothing.
  - If DB is empty/uninitialized and JSONL exists, import.
- Add migration/versioning:
  - DB schema version stored in metadata; handle upgrades safely.
- Tests / acceptance checks
  - Running worklog create then a separate worklog list shows the created item without relying on in-process state.
  - If .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is modified externally (simulate git pull), the next CLI/API startup refreshes DB and reflects the updated data.
  - If DB has newer data than JSONL, it does not overwrite DB (unless explicitly commanded); behavior is documented.
Acceptance criteria
- DB persists across separate CLI executions (verified by creating an item, exiting, re-running list/show).
- On startup (CLI + API), if .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is newer than DB state, DB is refreshed from JSONL automatically.
- No data loss when switching from current JSONL-only workflow: existing .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl is imported into the new DB on first run.
- Clear documented “source of truth” and when JSONL is written/updated.
Notes / implementation preference
- SQLite is a good default (single file on disk, easy distribution, supports concurrency better than ad-hoc JSON).
- Keep .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl for Git-friendly sharing, but treat it as an import/export boundary rather than the primary store.
data.title: Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer

data.description:
Summary
- Update the `wl next` selection logic to treat `updatedAt` (modification time) as a configurable signal (recency boost or penalty) and move from simple priority+createdAt tie-breaking to a multi-factor scoring function.

Why
- Current algorithm uses priority and creation time only (see `src/database.ts::selectHighestPriorityOldest`) which makes creation time the dominant tie-breaker. That causes recently-updated items to not be surfaced appropriately and encourages gaming by creating older stubs.
- Modification time (`updatedAt`) is a valuable signal: it can indicate recent discussion (should often be de-prioritized briefly) or recent activity requiring follow-up (should be surfaced). Making it configurable avoids hard assumptions.

Files of interest
- src/commands/next.ts
- src/database.ts

Proposed changes
1. Add a modular scoring function `computeScore(item, now, options)` that combines:
   - priority (primary)
   - due date proximity (if present)
   - blocked status (large negative if blocked)
   - assignee match (boost if assigned to current user)
   - effort (smaller items encouraged)
   - age (createdAt; small boost to older items to avoid starvation)
   - updatedAt recency: configurable as either a penalty for very recent updates or a boost for recent updates (policy option)
2. Replace `selectHighestPriorityOldest` and related selection points with `selectByScore(items, opts)` using the scoring function. Keep a stable tie-breaker (createdAt then id).
3. Add CLI flags to `wl next`:
   - `--recency-policy <prefer|avoid|ignore>` (default: avoid) to choose how updatedAt affects score
   - optional weight flags (advanced) or use config file to tune weights
4. Add unit tests covering:
   - prefer older items when priorities equal
   - penalize items edited in the last X hours (avoid)
   - prefer recently-updated items when policy=prefer
   - behavior with blocked/critical items remains unchanged
5. Document the behavior change in CLI.md and RELEASE notes.

Acceptance criteria
- `wl next` uses the scoring function and yields deterministic, explainable selection reasons
- New CLI flag `--recency-policy` works and is documented
- Tests added for core scoring behaviors

Notes
- This is non-destructive; default behavior should match existing behavior closely (use small age boost and a modest recent-update penalty by default).
- I will implement the change and include tests if you want; please confirm whether default `recency-policy` should be `avoid` (recommended) or `prefer`.
data.title: Improve 'wl next' selection algorithm to include modification time and scoring

Summary

Provide a new UI for updating a work-item's stage (and related fields) inspired by the existing close UI. The initial scope is to allow changing the stage of an item, but the component must be designed to grow to support other quick edits (status, comments, assignees, tags) so the keyboard shortcut and UX are generic. Suggest the primary keyboard shortcut be `U` (for Update) and follow existing patterns used by the close UI.

User stories

- As a Producer or Agent, I want to quickly change an item's stage (eg. idea -> in_progress -> review) without opening a full edit page so I can triage and advance work more efficiently.
- As a keyboard-focused user, I want a single, discoverable shortcut (`U`) to open a compact, accessible modal/popover to make quick changes.
- As a developer, I want a reusable component that can later include status changes, adding comments, and other small edits without a large refactor.

Expected behavior

- Pressing `U` when a work-item is focused opens the Update UI (modal or popover) similar in layout and affordances to the close UI.
- The UI shows the current stage, a list/dropdown of available stages (respecting permissions), and a Confirm/Cancel action.
- Choosing a new stage and confirming updates the work-item and closes the UI. The change should be optimistic or show a short saving state and surface errors.
- The UI should be accessible (keyboard navigable, ARIA roles) and mobile-friendly.

Suggested implementation approach

- Reuse the close UI component patterns: same modal/popover wrapper, header, action layout, and keyboard handling where appropriate.
- Implement a generic `QuickEdit` or `UpdatePanel` component with a small API that supports multiple field types (stage, status, inline comment). Initially only implement the `stage` field.
- Wire the `U` keyboard shortcut to open the component when a work-item row/card is focused. Keep the shortcut registration centralized so future quick-actions can share shortcuts.
- Ensure server API call is the same as used by the full edit flow (reuse existing update endpoint) and that the frontend updates local store/cache appropriately.
- Add unit and integration tests for the component and keyboard shortcut behavior.

Acceptance criteria

1. New work item (feature) exists in Worklog for this task.
2. Pressing `U` opens an Update UI for the focused item.
3. The UI allows selecting a new stage and confirms the change via the existing update API.
4. The UI handles success and error states and is keyboard accessible.
5. Code is implemented as a reusable component that can be extended to other quick edits.
6. Tests cover the main flows and the keyboard shortcut.

Notes / Risks / Dependencies

- Depends on existing close UI patterns; developer should review `Close` UI implementation for consistency.
- Permission checks: only allow stage changes for users with the required permissions; surface a message if not allowed.
- Decide whether `U` conflicts with other shortcuts; coordinate with global shortcut registry.

Suggested priority: medium
data.title: Add 'Update' UI to change work-item stage (shortcut: U)

Summary:
Replace the current Tab-based focus advancement in the affected component with Alt+Right Arrow. This work item updates the intended keyboard shortcut and documents expected behaviour and acceptance criteria.

Context:
The component currently advances focus with the Tab key. We want to change the shortcut to Alt+Right Arrow to avoid interfering with native Tab behaviour (sequential focus navigation) and to provide a more explicit, single-key modifier shortcut for this specific action.

User Stories:
- As a keyboard user, I can press Alt+Right Arrow to move the component's internal focus to the next interactive element without changing global Tab order.
- As a user relying on standard Tab navigation, pressing Tab should retain default browser/system behaviour and not trigger the component-specific focus advance.

Expected behaviour:
- Pressing Alt+Right Arrow moves focus to the next logical interactive element within the component.
- Pressing Alt+Left Arrow (if applicable) should move focus to the previous element (if this pattern exists today; if not, consider whether to implement a symmetric shortcut).
- Tab and Shift+Tab continue to perform standard sequential focus navigation and do not trigger the component-specific action.
- Shortcut should be documented in the component's accessibility notes and any visible hints/tooltips where applicable.

Steps to reproduce (before change):
1. Open the component UI that currently uses Tab to advance internal focus.
2. Press Tab and observe the component-specific focus change.

Suggested implementation approach:
- Update the component's keyboard handler to listen for Alt+Right Arrow (e.g. check for `event.altKey && event.key === 'ArrowRight'`) and call the existing focus-advance logic.
- Ensure the handler prevents default only when the Alt+Right combination is used; do not prevent default on plain Tab/Shift+Tab.
- Add unit and keyboard-integration tests to verify behaviour (Alt+Right advances focus; Tab does not trigger the component-specific advance).
- Update documentation and release notes to call out the new shortcut.

Acceptance criteria:
- The work item demonstrates a code change (or spec change) where Alt+Right Arrow is used to advance focus.
- Tests validating the new behaviour are added or updated.
- Documentation (component docs or accessibility notes) is updated to reference Alt+Right Arrow.
- No regression in standard Tab/Shift+Tab focus behaviour.

Notes:
- If other shortcuts use Alt+Right Arrow in the app, evaluate conflicts and adjust accordingly.
- Consider whether Alt+Left Arrow should be implemented for backward navigation and whether it should be part of this ticket or a follow-up.
data.title: Use Alt+Right Arrow to advance focus (replace Tab)

Summary:
Provide a template-driven validation system for Worklog so work items meet minimum content requirements and enforce defaults and limits for field values. Templates define required fields, types, default values, bounds, and regex/format constraints. Validation runs on create/update and can be applied retroactively.

User stories:
- As a contributor I want new work items to require the fields my team needs (e.g., summary, acceptance criteria, effort) so items are actionable.
- As a producer I want to enforce value limits (e.g., effort range, tag whitelist) and provide defaults for missing fields to reduce friction.
- As an operator I want to validate existing items against a template and receive a report of violations.

Expected behaviour:
- Templates are stored (YAML/JSON) and can be managed via the `wl` CLI: `wl template add|update|remove|list|show` and `wl template set-default <name>`.
- On `wl create` and `wl update` the CLI validates input against the active template and returns human-friendly errors for missing/invalid fields.
- Templates define: required fields, field types, default values, min/max for numeric fields, max-length for strings, allowed values (enums), regex patterns, and whether a field is editable after creation.
- Defaults are applied automatically when creating an item unless `--no-defaults` is passed.
- Provide a `wl template validate --report` command to check existing items and output a machine-readable report (JSON) and human summary.
- Validation is configurable per-project or global and supports template inheritance/variants (e.g., `bug`, `feature`, `chore`).

Suggested implementation approach:
- Add a `templates` store in the Worklog data model; templates versioned and referenced by work items.
- Implement a validation engine using JSON Schema or a small custom validator that supports the required rules and default application.
- Integrate validation into CLI create/update paths; fail fast with clear messages and exit codes suitable for automation.
- Provide tooling to scan and report violations and a migration assistant to fill defaults and flag unsafe auto-fixes.
- Add tests for schema parsing, CLI validation messages, and the validation report command.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A feature work item exists and is linked as a child of WL-0MKVZ55PR0LTMJA1.
2) CLI commands to manage templates are specified and implemented docs drafted.
3) `wl create` and `wl update` validate against the active template, applying defaults and rejecting invalid values with actionable errors.
4) `wl template validate` reports violations for existing items and supports a `--fix` mode that applies safe defaults after review.
5) Tests cover validator behavior, default application, and report generation.

data.description:
## Problem
Users need predictable, customizable sort order for work items representing actual work sequence. Current priority/date ordering doesn't capture nuanced sequencing needs, and custom ordering decisions cannot be persisted.

## Users
- **Contributors**: Need work items in execution order to pick next task efficiently
- **Producers**: Need to set/maintain custom ordering reflecting untracked dependencies and priorities
- **Team members**: Need consistent, deterministic ordering across views for planning

## Success criteria
- `wl list` and `wl next` return items in a consistent, deterministic order based on `sort_index` field
- Users can reorder items using `wl move` commands with changes persisted to database
- Custom order is maintained across filters unless explicitly overridden with `--sort` flag
- TUI supports interactive reordering with keyboard shortcuts
- Migration preserves logical ordering of existing items using current "next item" calculation logic
- System handles up to 1000 items per hierarchy level efficiently
- Sort order syncs correctly across team members via Git
- Documentation updated to explain new sort behavior and commands
- Regression tests added for sort operations

## Constraints
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing CLI commands
- Sort_index gaps must use large intervals (100s) to minimize reindexing
- Parent items moving must bring their children as a group
- Reindexing on sync must preserve relative ordering while resolving conflicts
- Database schema changes require migration for existing installations
- Performance must remain acceptable for up to 1000 items per level

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk**: Migration failure could corrupt existing work item ordering
- **Risk**: Concurrent edits by multiple users could create sort_index conflicts
- **Risk**: Large hierarchies (>1000 items) may experience performance degradation
- **Risk**: Gap exhaustion between frequently reordered items may trigger frequent reindexing
- **Assumption**: Current "next item" logic can be extracted and reused for sort calculation
- **Assumption**: SQLite can efficiently handle index-based sorting at scale
- **Assumption**: Users will understand the difference between custom order and priority-based order
- **Mitigation**: Include rollback capability in migration script
- **Mitigation**: Add performance benchmarks before/after implementation

## Existing state
- Work items currently ordered by combination of priority and creation date
- No persistent custom ordering capability
- `wl list` and `wl next` use different ordering logic
- No ability to manually reorder items
- TUI displays items in tree structure but doesn't support reordering

## Desired change
- Add integer `sort_index` field to work items table
- Implement hierarchical sorting where items are ordered by sort_index within their level
- Add CLI commands: `wl move <id> --before <id>` and `wl move <id> --after <id>`
- Calculate initial sort_index values using existing "next item" calculation logic applied hierarchically (level 0 items first, then level 1 under each parent, etc.)
- New items inserted at appropriate position using same "next item" calculation for their hierarchy level
- Add TUI keyboard shortcuts for interactive reordering (accessible to all users)
- Implement both automatic and manual (`wl move auto`) redistribution when gaps exhausted
- Add `--sort` flag to override default ordering (e.g., `--sort=priority`, `--sort=created`)
- Reindex automatically after sync operations to resolve conflicts

## Likely duplicates / related docs
- README.md (contains existing CLI command documentation)
- src/database.ts (database schema and operations)
- src/commands/list.ts (current list implementation)
- src/commands/helpers.ts (likely contains sorting/next item logic)
- src/commands/next.ts (next item selection logic to extract)
- src/tui/components/ (TUI components for keyboard interaction)
- AGENTS.md (work item management documentation)

## Related work items
- WL-0MKVZ55PR0LTMJA1: Epic: CLI usability & output (parent epic)
- WL-0MKWYVATG0G0I029: Sort order for work item list (current work item/user story)

## Recommended next step
NEW PRD at: docs/prd/sort_order_PRD.md (no existing PRD found for this feature)
data.title: Implement sort_index field and custom ordering for work items

Summary:
Currently the opencode prompt input box is resized when the user explicitly triggers a resize (e.g. Ctrl+Enter), but it does NOT resize when a typed line naturally word-wraps to the next visual line. This causes the input box to overflow or hide content and makes editing large multi-line prompts awkward.

Expected behaviour:
- The prompt input box should automatically expand vertically when the current input wraps onto additional visual lines, keeping the caret and the newly wrapped content visible.
- Manual resize on Ctrl+Enter should continue to work as before.
- Expansion should be bounded by a sensible maximum (e.g. a configurable max rows or available terminal height) and fall back to scrolling within the input if the maximum is reached.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Typing a long line that word-wraps causes the input box to grow to accommodate the wrapped lines up to the configured max height.
2) When max height is reached, additional wrapped content scrolls inside the input box rather than being clipped off-screen.
3) Ctrl+Enter manual resize remains functional and consistent with automatic resize.

data.description:
Implement real-time progress feedback for OpenCode interactions in the TUI by displaying current activity status and using visual indicators.

## Context

The TUI currently shows basic 'waiting' indicator in prompt label when OpenCode is processing. This work item enhances that to provide richer, real-time feedback about what OpenCode is doing.

Related Work Items:
- Parent: WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2 (Epic: Platform - TUI)
- Related: WL-0MKW7SLB30BFCL5O (Epic: Opencode server + interactive 'O' pane) - completed
- Discovered-from: Recent commit 1826786 (blocking duplicate prompts)

Related Files:
- src/commands/tui.ts (lines ~973-1270: SSE event handling in connectToSSE function)
- docs/opencode-tui.md (TUI documentation)

## Problem

Users cannot see what OpenCode is currently doing when processing requests. The only feedback is a generic '(waiting...)' label. This creates uncertainty about whether OpenCode is thinking, reading files, writing code, or stuck.

## Solution

Enhance progress feedback using OpenCode's SSE event stream:

### 1. Response Pane Header Progress (Moderate Detail)
Display current activity in the response pane's title/header area:
- Update on activity change only (not every text chunk)
- Show moderate detail: 'Thinking...', 'Using tool: read', 'Writing files', 'Running command'
- Clear when operation completes

### 2. Prompt Label Spinner
Add animated Braille dots spinner after 'waiting' text:
- Pattern: ⠋ ⠙ ⠹ ⠸ ⠼ ⠴ ⠦ ⠧ ⠇ ⠏
- Shows during any processing activity
- Stops and clears when ready

### 3. Inline Messages (Detailed, Selective)
Insert detailed messages into response stream for:
- File operations: '[Writing: src/file.ts]', '[Editing: package.json]', '[Deleted: temp.js]'
- Questions/input requests: Already handled, ensure formatting consistency

## Event Types to Handle

Based on OpenCode SSE stream analysis:

### session.status (Primary State Indicator)
- status.type: 'busy' → Show spinner + activity
- status.type: 'idle' → Clear progress, stop spinner

Example events:
```json
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "busy"}}}
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "idle"}}}
{"type": "session.status", "properties": {"sessionId": "abc123", "status": {"type": "busy", "activity": "thinking"}}}
```

### message.part.updated (Activity Details)
- part.type: 'text' → Header: 'Writing response...'
- part.type: 'tool-use' + tool.name → Header: 'Using tool: {name}', Inline: '[Using {name}: {description}]' (for file ops only)
- part.type: 'tool-result' → Header: 'Processing result...', Inline: Show file ops results
- part.type: 'step-start' → Header: Show step description

Example events:
```json
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "text", "text": "Let me help...", "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-use", "tool": {"name": "read", "description": "Reading file.ts"}, "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-use", "tool": {"name": "write", "description": "Writing src/test.ts"}, "messageID": "m1"}}}
{"type": "message.part.updated", "properties": {"part": {"type": "tool-result", "content": "File written successfully", "messageID": "m1"}}}
```

### message.updated (Message Lifecycle)
- Track message completion via time.completed field
- Clear progress when assistant message completes

Example events:
```json
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m1", "role": "assistant", "time": {"started": 1234567890}}}}
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m1", "role": "assistant", "time": {"started": 1234567890, "completed": 1234567900}}}}
{"type": "message.updated", "properties": {"info": {"id": "m2", "role": "user", "time": {"started": 1234567880, "completed": 1234567881}}}}
```

### question.asked (Already Handled)
- Ensure inline message formatting is consistent
- Example already in code at line ~1154

## Implementation Approach

1. Add spinner animation to prompt label
   - Use setInterval for Braille dots animation
   - Start when isWaitingForResponse = true
   - Stop when isWaitingForResponse = false
   - Update label: 'OpenCode (waiting {spinner})' or 'OpenCode Prompt'

2. Add activity tracking in connectToSSE
   - Track current activity state (idle, thinking, using_tool, writing, etc.)
   - Add function to update response pane title/label based on activity
   - Update only when activity changes (debounce)

3. Enhance event handlers (lines ~1053-1253)
   - session.status: Update activity state, start/stop spinner
   - message.part.updated: Update activity based on part.type and tool.name
   - For write/edit/delete tools: append inline message to stream
   - message.updated: Check for completion, clear progress

4. Add cleanup on operation complete
   - Reset activity state to idle
   - Stop spinner animation
   - Clear response pane header progress
   - Restore default labels

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Response pane header shows current activity (thinking, using tool: X, writing, etc.)
- [ ] Activity updates on state change only, not on every text chunk (smooth performance)
- [ ] Prompt label shows animated Braille dots spinner during processing
- [ ] Spinner stops when operation completes or errors
- [ ] File operations (write, edit, delete) show inline messages with file names
- [ ] Questions/input requests display with consistent inline formatting
- [ ] No UI flickering or performance degradation during high-frequency SSE events
- [ ] Progress indicators clear properly when operation completes
- [ ] No regressions to existing features (autocomplete, input requests, streaming, etc.)
- [ ] Code follows existing TUI patterns and blessed.js conventions

## Testing

Manual testing:
1. Open TUI, press 'o' to open OpenCode
2. Send prompt: 'Read the package.json file and tell me the version'
   - Verify spinner appears in prompt label
   - Verify header shows 'Using tool: read'
   - Verify response streams correctly
   - Verify spinner stops when complete

3. Send prompt: 'Create a new file test.ts with a hello function'
   - Verify header shows 'Using tool: write'
   - Verify inline message: '[Writing: test.ts]'
   - Verify spinner animation is smooth
   - Verify everything clears when done

4. Send prompt while previous is processing
   - Verify blocked with toast message (existing feature)
   - Verify spinner continues for original request

5. Test with rapid streaming (long response)
   - Verify no flickering or performance issues
   - Verify header updates appropriately

data.description:
Summary:
Provide a keyboard-driven way in the TUI to reparent (move) worklog items without copying or typing item IDs.

User story:
As a user of the TUI, I want to move an item to a different parent without having to copy or manually type any worklog IDs, so I can reorganize items quickly using only keyboard (or mouse) selection.

Expected behaviour:
- The user selects an item in the TUI (the item to move).
- The user triggers a move action (suggested key: `m`).
- The UI enters a move-target selection mode (visually highlighted), allowing the user to select a new parent item.
- The user confirms the target by hitting the same key again (or an explicit Confirm action).
- The client performs `wl update <source-id> --parent <target-id>` and updates the UI to reflect the new parent.
- The action is cancellable (Esc or explicit Cancel) and shows a small confirmation/undo affordance or success/failure message.

Acceptance criteria (testable):
1) Start from any TUI view that lists items. Select an item and press the move key; the UI clearly indicates move mode.
2) Selecting a target and confirming runs the equivalent `wl update <source> --parent <target>` and the item appears under the new parent in the UI.
3) Cancelling move mode leaves items unchanged and returns the UI to normal navigation.
4) Errors from `wl update` are surfaced to the user (eg. invalid target, permissions) and the UI remains consistent.
5) The feature can be exercised entirely with keyboard (mouse selection may be supported but not required).

Suggested implementation details (proposal, not prescriptive):
- Add a move-mode state to the TUI. When active, the selected source item is stored and the UI highlights potential target items.
- Use a single key to toggle move-mode and also confirm the selection (eg. `m` to start, `m` to confirm). Allow Enter as alternative confirm.
- On confirm, run: `wl update <SOURCE-ID> --parent <TARGET-ID>` using existing client logic that issues wl commands. Show a short success or error toast.
- Provide clear visual affordances: source highlight, target highlight, instructions in the footer ("Move mode: select target and press 'm' to confirm; Esc to cancel").
- Consider multi-select or batch move as future enhancement (out-of-scope for initial implementation).

Notes:
- This request is intentionally flexible about exact keybindings or UI details — the above is a suggested flow. Other UXs that avoid typing IDs are acceptable.

Related tags: tui, ux, feature
data.title: TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs

4) Errors from `wl update` are surfaced to the user and the UI remains consistent.
5) The feature can be exercised entirely with keyboard.

Suggested implementation details:
- Add a move-mode state to the TUI. When active, the selected source item is stored and the UI highlights potential target items.
- Use a single key to toggle move-mode and also confirm the selection (eg. `m` to start, `m` to confirm). Allow Enter as alternative confirm.
- On confirm, run: `wl update <SOURCE-ID> --parent <TARGET-ID>` using existing client logic that issues wl commands. Show a short success or error toast.
- Provide clear visual affordances: source highlight, target highlight, instructions in the footer ("Move mode: select target and press 'm' to confirm; Esc to cancel").
- Consider multi-select or batch move as future enhancement (out-of-scope for initial implementation).

Notes:
- This request is intentionally flexible about exact keybindings or UI details — the above is a suggested flow. Other UXs that avoid typing IDs are acceptable.

When wl init runs in a new git worktree, it incorrectly places .worklog in the main repository instead of the worktree. 

The issue is in resolveWorklogDir() in src/worklog-paths.ts. Currently, the function uses git rev-parse --show-toplevel which returns the main repository root even when called from within a worktree. This causes all worktrees to share the same .worklog directory, leading to data conflicts and initialization failures.

The solution is to detect when we're in a git worktree (by checking if .git is a file rather than a directory) and skip the repo-root .worklog lookup in that case.

## Acceptance Criteria
- wl init in a new worktree places .worklog in the worktree directory, not the main repo
- wl init in the main repository still places .worklog in the main repo
- wl init in a subdirectory of the main repo finds the repo-root .worklog if it exists
- Each worktree maintains independent worklog state
- All existing tests pass
- Code handles both main repos and worktrees correctly

## Testing Scenarios
1. Initialize worklog in main repo - .worklog created in main repo root
2. Initialize worklog in existing worktree - .worklog created in worktree root
3. Run wl commands in worktree - uses worktree's .worklog, not main repo's
4. Switch between worktrees - each maintains separate state

## Related Files
- src/worklog-paths.ts (getRepoRoot, resolveWorklogDir)
- src/config.ts (uses resolveWorklogDir)
- tests/ (add worktree-specific tests)

# Intake Brief: Extend Update Dialog (Phase 2)

## Problem Statement

The current Update dialog (Phase 1, WL-0MKVYN4HW1AMQFAV) only supports quick stage changes via the `U` keyboard shortcut. Users need to quickly modify multiple essential work-item fields (status, priority, and add comments) without opening a full edit page. This phase extends the dialog to support these common quick-edits while maintaining keyboard accessibility and a compact UX.

## Users & User Stories

- **Producer/Agent triaging work:** As a producer, I want to quickly update a work-item's status and priority from the TUI list view (e.g., mark as blocked, escalate priority, add a note) without leaving the tree view.
- **Keyboard-focused user:** As a keyboard-first TUI user, I want to make multiple field changes in a single dialog session and submit them together (e.g., change stage to in_progress, status to open, and add a comment all at once).
- **Busy team lead:** As a team lead reviewing work-items, I want to add quick comments (multi-line notes) to items without switching contexts.

## Expected Behavior

- Pressing `U` with a work-item focused opens the expanded Update dialog.
- The dialog shows all fields: **stage** (existing), **status**, **priority**, and **comment**.
- All fields are visible in a single dialog (expanded height as needed).
- User navigates via Tab/Shift-Tab to select a field, arrow keys to navigate options, Enter to confirm selection.
- Status/stage combinations are validated (e.g., warn if user selects conflicting status/stage pairs like status=open + stage=done).
- Comment is a multi-line text box embedded in the dialog.
- On submit, all selected changes are sent in a single API call (reusing existing db.update).
- Dialog shows success feedback (toast) or errors if the update fails.
- Dialog remains keyboard accessible, mobile-friendly, and consistent with existing TUI patterns.

## Constraints

- Dialog must remain usable in typical terminal windows; both height (currently 14) and width (currently 50%) will need to increase to accommodate multiple fields and multi-line comment input. Consider reasonable maximums (e.g., 60% width, ~20-25 lines height) and plan for graceful degradation in smaller terminals.
- Only status, priority, and comment are in scope; **parent field is deferred to Phase 3**.
- Keyboard navigation must follow existing TUI patterns (Tab, arrow keys, Enter) used by the close dialog.
- Status/stage validation must happen on the frontend (show which combinations are invalid) to prevent backend errors.

## Existing State

- Phase 1 (WL-0MKVYN4HW1AMQFAV) implemented the basic Update dialog with stage-only quick-edit via the `U` shortcut.
- `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts:102–139` defines the update dialog structure; currently shows only stage options and is 14 lines tall.
- Tests exist (`tests/tui/tui-update-dialog.test.ts`) that verify stage-change updates via db.update().
- The close dialog (lines 63–99) provides a UX/pattern reference for how to structure the multi-option dialog.

## Desired Change

1. Extend `updateDialog` and `updateDialogOptions` in `dialogs.ts` to display and manage status, priority, and comment fields.
2. Increase dialog height and implement field navigation (Tab selects field, arrow keys navigate options within field, Enter confirms).
3. Add frontend validation logic to prevent invalid status/stage combinations; surface warnings in the UI.
4. Implement a multi-line comment input box within the dialog using blessed text input or similar.
5. Update the keyboard shortcut handler to collect changes from all fields and submit as a single db.update call.
6. Extend test coverage to verify multi-field edits, status/stage validation, and comment addition.
7. Update any documentation or in-TUI help text to reflect the new fields.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MKVYN4HW1AMQFAV** (Phase 1 - completed): Initial stage-only Update dialog implementation.
- **WL-0MKWDOMSL0B4UAZX** (completed): Tests for TUI quick-edit via shortcut U.
- **WL-0MKVZ5TN71L3YPD1** (parent epic): TUI UX improvements.
- **Document:** `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts` — Update dialog component.
- **Document:** `tests/tui/tui-update-dialog.test.ts` — Update dialog test patterns.

## Success Criteria

1. Update dialog displays status, priority, and comment fields alongside stage.
2. User can navigate fields with Tab/Shift-Tab and select options with arrow keys and Enter.
3. Status/stage combination validation is enforced (invalid combinations are disabled or warned about).
4. Multi-line comment text can be entered and submitted with other field changes.
5. All field changes are sent in a single db.update call and persist correctly.
6. Dialog is keyboard accessible and follows existing TUI keyboard patterns.
7. Tests cover multi-field edits, validation logic, and comment addition.
8. Dialog grows appropriately in both height and width; consider reasonable maximums (e.g., 60% width, ~20-25 lines height) with graceful degradation for smaller terminals.
9. Success/error feedback is shown to user (toast or dialog message).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Dialog height and width may become unwieldy if not carefully designed. **Mitigation:** Plan layout carefully; consider field grouping or scrolling within the dialog if needed. Start with reasonable dimensions (e.g., 60% width, ~20-25 lines) and adjust based on usability testing.
- **Assumption:** Status/stage combinations have well-defined rules in the codebase (e.g., only certain status values are valid for each stage). **Mitigation:** Verify these rules exist and document them before implementing validation.
- **Assumption:** The existing db.update API accepts multiple field changes in one call. **Mitigation:** Confirm this is supported; if not, batch calls or refactor the API.
- **Risk:** Comment input may conflict with dialog keyboard navigation (e.g., Tab inside comment box vs. Tab to next field). **Mitigation:** Use a blessed Box or similar that respects parent modal focus; test thoroughly.

## Suggested Next Step

Proceed to **Planning Phase**: Break this work into discrete sub-tasks (e.g., extend dialog UI, implement field navigation, add validation, implement comment input, add tests, update docs) and create child work-items for each sub-task.

## Problem

Work items with 'in-progress' status are not appearing blue in the TUI tree view, despite having the correct status. This affects WL-0ML16W7000D2M8J3 and other in-progress items.

## Root Cause

The titleColorForStatus() function in src/commands/helpers.ts uses chalk to generate ANSI color codes, but blessed's list component doesn't properly interpret ANSI codes in text strings. Blessed expects its own markup tags (e.g. {cyan-fg}text{/cyan-fg}) instead.

When colored text with ANSI codes is passed to blessed, the codes are lost or misinterpreted, causing the TUI list to not display the correct colors.

## Solution

Replace chalk color codes with blessed markup tags in the titleColorForStatus() and renderTitle() functions. This allows blessed's built-in tag parser (tags: true is already enabled on the list component) to properly render the colors.

The mapping should be:
- 'in-progress' → {cyan-fg}text{/cyan-fg} (was chalk.cyan)
- 'completed' → {gray-fg}text{/gray-fg} (was chalk.gray)
- 'blocked' → {red-fg}text{/red-fg} (was chalk.redBright)
- 'open' (default) → {green-fg}text{/green-fg} (was chalk.greenBright)

Note: This change only affects TUI output. Other uses of chalk in helpers.ts (console output, conflict resolution display) should remain unchanged since those aren't going to blessed.

## Related Files

- src/commands/helpers.ts - titleColorForStatus() and renderTitle() functions (lines 61-80)
- src/commands/tui.ts - uses formatTitleOnly() to render tree items (line 949)
- src/tui/components/list.ts - blessed list component with tags: true enabled (line 24)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Work items with 'in-progress' status appear cyan/blue in the TUI tree view
2. Work items with 'completed' status appear gray in the TUI tree view
3. Work items with 'blocked' status appear red in the TUI tree view
4. Work items with 'open' status appear green in the TUI tree view (or other default color)
5. WL-0ML16W7000D2M8J3 now appears blue in the tree
6. All existing tests pass
7. No changes to console output formatting (chalk usage outside TUI remains unchanged)
data.title: Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes
