Problem statement
The Worklog CLI lacks a dependency management command, preventing users from recording and inspecting dependency edges via the CLI. This intake defines a minimal `wl dep` command set and outputs to enable dependency tracking workflows without edge types.

Users
- Developers and agents managing work items who need to declare and view dependencies from the CLI.
- Maintainers who need a human-readable and JSON output for automation.

User stories
- As a developer, I want to add a dependency so I can track what blocks a work item.
- As a maintainer, I want to list both inbound and outbound dependencies so I can see what is blocked and what is blocking.
- As an automation user, I want JSON output with key fields to parse dependencies programmatically.

Success criteria
- `wl dep add <item> <depends-on>` creates a dependency edge where item depends on depends-on.
- `wl dep rm <item> <depends-on>` removes the dependency edge if present.
- `wl dep list <item>` shows two sections: “Depends on” and “Depended on by”, even when empty.
- Human output lists ids, titles, status, priority, and direction; JSON includes the same fields.
- Missing ids produce warnings and the command exits 0.

Constraints
- No dependency types or type validation.
- Minimal CLI surface (add/rm/list only) with existing global flags support (e.g., --json).
- Non-destructive behavior for missing ids (warn and continue).

Existing state
- Worklog has blocked status handling and parses blocking ids from descriptions/comments.
- No `wl dep` CLI exists in `CLI.md`, and no dependency edge storage is implemented in code.

Desired change
- Implement `wl dep add|rm|list` commands for dependency edges without types.
- Ensure list output includes inbound and outbound sections with detailed fields.
- Add warnings for missing ids without failing the command.

Related work
- WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US — Add wl dep command (this intake)
- WL-0ML4PH4EQ1XODFM0 — Doctor: detect missing dep references (child item)
- WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6 — Feature: worklog doctor (integrity checks)
- `CLI.md` — CLI reference, currently missing dep command

Suggested next step
- Proceed to the five review passes for this intake draft, then update WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US with the approved brief.

# Intake Brief: Standardize Status/Stage Labels From Config

## Problem Statement
Status and stage labels (and their legal combinations) are currently hard-coded in the TUI, creating inconsistent formatting and a split source of truth across TUI and CLI. This work makes labels and compatibility config-driven so both TUI and CLI render and validate against one shared, repo-specific definition.

## Users
- Contributors and agents who update work items via TUI or CLI and need consistent labels and rules.

### Example user stories
- As a contributor, I want status/stage labels to be consistent and configurable so TUI/CLI use a single source of truth.

## Success Criteria
- Status and stage labels and compatibility rules are sourced from `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`.
- TUI update dialog renders labels from config and validates status/stage compatibility using config rules.
- CLI `wl create` and `wl update` reject invalid status/stage combinations with a clear error listing valid options.
- CLI accepts kebab-case values that map to valid snake_case values, with a warning on conversion.
- No remaining hard-coded status/stage label or compatibility arrays in the TUI/CLI code path.

## Constraints
- No backward compatibility: remove hard-coded defaults; if config is missing required sections, fail with a clear error.
- Canonical values and labels use `snake_case`.
- Compatibility is defined in one direction in config (status -> allowed stages); derive the reverse mapping in code.
- If CLI inputs are kebab-case equivalents of valid values, accept with warning; otherwise reject with error.
- Doctor validation depends on this config work landing first.

## Existing State
- TUI uses hard-coded status/stage values and compatibility in `src/tui/status-stage-rules.ts` and validation helpers.
- Inventory exists in `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` describing current rules and gaps.

## Desired Change
- Extend config schema to include status labels, stage labels, and status->stage compatibility in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`.
- Refactor TUI update dialog and validation helpers to read labels and compatibility from config.
- Refactor CLI create/update flows to validate status/stage compatibility from config, including kebab-case normalization with warnings.
- Remove hard-coded status/stage labels and compatibility arrays from TUI/CLI runtime path.

## Risks & Assumptions
- Risk: Existing work items may contain invalid status/stage values and will fail validation; remediation will be required.
- Risk: Missing config sections will cause immediate failure by design.
- Assumption: Config defaults will include the full, canonical status/stage values and compatibility mapping.
- Assumption: `snake_case` is the canonical value format for statuses and stages.

## Related Work
- Standardize status/stage labels from config (WL-0ML4CQ8QL03P215I)
- Validation rules inventory (WL-0ML4W3B5E1IAXJ1P)
- Doctor: validate status/stage values from config (WL-0MLE6WJUY0C5RRVX)
- wl doctor (WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6)
- `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` — current rules and gaps
- `src/tui/status-stage-rules.ts` — current hard-coded values and compatibility

## Suggested Next Step
Proceed to review and approval of this intake draft, then run the five review passes (completeness, capture fidelity, related-work & traceability, risks & assumptions, polish & handoff) before updating the work item description.

User story: As a user, I want the reason for selection text to wrap within the dialog so I can read long reasons without overflow or truncation.

Behavior:
- Reason text in the next work item dialog wraps to the available width.
- No horizontal scrolling or overflow for long reason strings.
- Layout remains readable on common dialog widths.

Acceptance criteria:
- Long reason strings wrap onto multiple lines.
- Dialog layout stays intact across typical window sizes.
- No text overlap with other fields or actions.
data.title: Wrap selection reason text in work item dialog

data.description:
Summary: The Update dialog does not offer the 'intake_release' stage option, preventing users from selecting it.

User story:
- As a TUI user, I need to set a work item stage to intake_release from the Update dialog.

Expected behavior:
- The Update dialog includes 'intake_release' in the stage options list.
- Validation rules allow appropriate status/stage combinations for intake_release.
- Selection and submission work the same as other stages.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Update dialog displays 'intake_release' as a selectable stage option.
2. Selecting 'intake_release' and submitting updates the work item stage successfully.
3. Status/stage compatibility reflects any rules for intake_release (if applicable).
4. Tests are updated or added to cover the new stage option.

Notes:
- Parent: WL-0MKXJEVY01VKXR4C
data.title: Add intake_release stage to Update dialog

data.description:
Summary: Extend wl dep list to support directional filtering for dependency edges.

User story:
- As an agent, I want to query only outbound dependencies for a work item so I can check whether a dependency edge already exists without client-side filtering.

Expected behavior:
- wl dep list <itemId> --outgoing --json returns only outbound edges (item depends on dependsOn).
- wl dep list <itemId> --incoming --json returns only inbound edges (items that depend on item).
- If neither flag is provided, retain current behavior (both directions).
- If both flags are provided, return an error (preferred behavior).
- JSON output shape unchanged aside from filtered contents.

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI help documents --outgoing and --incoming for wl dep list.
- Filtering works in both human and --json output.
- Unit tests cover outbound-only, inbound-only, and default behavior.
- Backward compatibility: existing usage without flags continues to work.

Notes:
- Ensure error messaging is clear when both flags are provided.
data.title: Add directional filtering to wl dep list

data.description:
Summary: Add a --body alias for wl comment add/create that maps to the existing --comment option.

User story:
- As an agent, I want to use --body when adding comments so CLI usage is consistent with other systems and less error-prone.

Expected behavior:

data.description:
Problem statement

When dependency edges are removed, or when an item that was blocking another moves to a non-blocking state, blocked items are not consistently returned to an unblocked status. This causes work to remain incorrectly marked as `blocked` and prevents it from being surfaced by `wl next` or other discovery flows.

Users

- Producer/triager: As a producer, I want blocked items to automatically become unblocked when their blockers are resolved so they reappear in work discovery.
- Developer/assignee: As an assignee, I want the item's status to reflect current reality without manual changes after blockers are removed.

Success criteria

- When a dependency is removed (via `wl dep rm`) a dependent item is marked `open` if no remaining active blockers exist.
- When a blocking item's stage or status changes to an inactive state (stage in `in_review` or `done`, or status `completed`/`deleted`) the dependent item is marked `open` if no other active blockers exist.
- The change is idempotent and makes no status change if other active blockers remain.
- Automated logic runs on dependency removal and on updates to work items that may affect blocking status.

Constraints

- Preserve existing `wl dep` behavior except add unblocking side-effects when appropriate.
- Do not change other status/stage semantics; use existing stage/status values as signals.
- Keep changes minimal: prefer simple `status` updates over storing historical status unless explicitly requested.

Existing state

- Dependency edges are persisted and exposed via `db.listDependencyEdgesFrom` / `listDependencyEdgesTo` (see `src/database.ts`).
- `wl dep add` and `wl dep rm` update work item statuses in some cases already (`src/commands/dep.ts`).
- `src/database.ts` contains helper functions to list dependency edges and to inspect items/comments for blocking references.

Desired change

- Add an idempotent reconciliation step that runs:
  - after `dep rm` completes and
  - whenever a work item is updated (status or stage changes) and that work item is the target of dependency edges.

- The reconciliation will:
  1. For each item that depends on the changed/removed item, collect all outbound dependency edges from that dependent item.
  2. Treat a dependency edge as inactive if the target item's stage is `in_review` or `done`, or its status is `completed` or `deleted`.
  3. If none of the remaining outbound dependencies are active blockers, update the dependent item's `status` to `open` (no status history restoration).
  4. If at least one active blocker remains, leave the dependent item `blocked`.

- Prefer small, testable helpers in `src/database.ts` (e.g., `getInboundDependents(id)`, `hasActiveBlockers(itemId)`), and call them from `dep rm` and from the general `update` path where status/stage changes are handled.

Related work

- WL-0ML4TFSQ70Y3UPMR `wl dep add/rm` — CLI surface implemented and partially updates status on add/rm.
- WL-0ML4TFSGF1SLN4DT `Persist dependency edges` — edge persistence is implemented and exported to JSONL.
- WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6 `Feature: worklog doctor` — integrity checks and periodic reconciliation may be relevant for a delayed fallback.

Suggested next step

1) Proceed to implement small database helpers and wire the reconciliation into `dep rm` and the item `update` path. Implementation includes unit tests for edge cases (multiple blockers, missing targets, already-open items).

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Race conditions if multiple updates/removals happen concurrently; Mitigation: Ensure database operations are atomic and write-through (DB layer functions call `exportToJsonl()` and `triggerAutoSync()` consistently).
- Risk: False unblocking if stage/status semantics change elsewhere; Mitigation: Keep the active-blocker definition centralized in DB helpers and document behavior.
- Assumption: Dependency edges are correctly persisted and queryable via existing store accessors.
data.title: Auto-unblock on dependency changes

data.description:
Summary:
Investigate and refactor long-running CLI tests to reduce test runtime and flakiness. Several CLI tests legitimately perform integration steps (git ops, file IO, DB exports) and take multiple seconds when run as part of the full suite. Increasing timeouts or running tests serially reduces flakes but is a workaround. This task scopes a refactor to mock/stub external dependencies and optimize test setup/teardown to make the CLI test suite fast and reliable without relying on serial execution or increased per-test timeouts.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- Identify the slow tests and the underlying reasons (git operations, DB file writes, external process spawning, plugin loading).
- Replace or mock external operations (git, file system heavy setups, remote sync) where feasible to reduce test duration.
- Where mocking is not feasible, move tests to an integration-only folder and ensure fast unit tests remain fast.
- Achieve full test-suite run time reduction of CLI tests by at least 30% on CI or reduce the number of tests that require >5s to run.
- Keep tests deterministic: run the full suite 3x under CI-like environment without intermittent timeouts.

Suggested implementation approach:
1) Audit tests to produce per-test timings and identify top slow tests.
2) For each slow test, attempt to stub external commands (spawn/exec) and external services or replace with in-memory equivalents.
3) Consolidate repeated heavy setup/teardown into shared fixtures (reusable temp dirs, seeded DB snapshots).
4) Add targeted unit tests if integration tests are split out.
5) Document CI changes or rerun strategies if needed.

Files/Areas to review:
- tests/cli/init.test.ts
- tests/cli/status.test.ts
- tests/cli/worktree.test.ts
- tests/cli/* helpers: tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts, tests/test-utils.js
- vitest.config.ts and CI scripts

Notes:
- This is a non-blocking task for WL-0MLB5ZIOO0BDJJPG; it is an improvement idea and should be evaluated for scope.,

data.description:
Summary

Navigation inside the "Update" window is inconsistent and fails for keyboard and mouse users. Some interactive areas (header toolbar, main editor, metadata panel, selection lists, and save/cancel controls) are not reachable or behave unexpectedly when using Tab/Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter/Escape, or mouse interactions. This causes friction when editing entries and risks data loss when navigation unexpectedly closes or blurs controls.

User story

As a user editing an entry in the Update window I want predictable keyboard and mouse navigation between all interactive areas and within each selection list so I can complete edits quickly and access all controls without losing focus or context.

Expected behaviour

- Opening the Update window sets focus to the primary editable control (title or main editor) and announces the dialog to assistive tech.
- Tab/Shift+Tab moves focus in a logical order through all interactive areas: header controls → main editor → selection list triggers → metadata panel controls → save/cancel → back to header (no hidden stops).
- Each selection list (dropdown or picker) supports keyboard interaction: open with Enter/Space, navigate options with ArrowUp/ArrowDown, confirm with Enter, close with Escape, and supports type-to-filter where applicable.
- When a selection list is opened focus is managed inside the list until it is closed; selecting an option returns focus to the list trigger and updates the displayed value.
- Mouse interactions open/close lists and set focus appropriately; clicking outside a list closes it without losing the current editing focus unless Save/Cancel are chosen.
- Navigation controls (Next/Previous item) move between items without losing unsaved data; if unsaved changes exist, a confirmation prompt appears.

Suggested approach

- Audit and enforce a consistent tab order for all controls in the Update window.
- Implement roving tabindex or ARIA menu/listbox patterns for selection lists to handle keyboard navigation and focus management.
- Ensure dialog semantics are correct (role=dialog, aria-modal if appropriate) and that the dialog is announced on open.
- Add automated and manual tests that validate keyboard/mouse navigation flows.

Acceptance criteria (tests)

Note: Run these tests manually and automate where feasible. For each test, include environment (desktop/mobile), expected result, and pass/fail.

1) Open behaviour
- Steps: Open the Update window from the list view.
- Expected: Focus lands on the primary editable control (title/main editor). Screen reader announces the dialog title and role.

2) Tab order across areas
- Steps: Press Tab repeatedly from the initial focus to cycle through the window, then Shift+Tab to go backwards.
- Expected: Focus visits, in order: header toolbar buttons (Back/Close), primary editor, each selection list trigger (Project, Type, Assignee, Tags), metadata panel fields, Save button, Cancel button, then back to header. No controls are skipped or unexpectedly focused.

3) Selection list: keyboard navigation
- Steps: Focus a selection list trigger and press Enter to open. Use ArrowDown/ArrowUp to move through options and press Enter to select.
- Expected: The list opens; arrow keys move the visible and screen-reader focus; Enter selects an option and the trigger reflects the selected value; focus returns to the trigger.

4) Selection list: type-to-filter
- Steps: Open a large selection list (≥10 items), type characters corresponding to an option, press Enter.
- Expected: The list filters or jumps to matching options, Enter selects the desired option, and focus returns to the trigger.

5) Selection list: mouse interactions
- Steps: Click a selection list trigger, click an option, click outside.
- Expected: Clicking opens the list; clicking an option selects it and closes the list; clicking outside closes the list without changing other controls' focus.

6) Selection list: Escape behaviour
- Steps: Open a list via keyboard, press Escape.
- Expected: The list closes and focus returns to the list trigger; no selection change occurs.

7) Focus management while list open
- Steps: Open a list and press Tab.
- Expected: If the design keeps focus within the list, Tab should move to the next focusable in the list; otherwise the list should close and focus continue to next window control. The behaviour must be consistent and documented; implement the option that matches existing app patterns (recommended: close on Tab and move to next control).

8) Next/Previous item navigation
- Steps: With the Update window open, use Next/Previous controls (or keyboard shortcuts if present) to navigate to the next/previous item.
- Expected: The window updates to show the next item; any unsaved changes trigger a confirmation before navigation; focus remains in the primary editable control for the new item.

9) Mobile/touch behaviour (where applicable)
- Steps: Open the Update window on a mobile viewport, interact with selection lists and metadata fields using touch.
- Expected: Touch opens and closes lists correctly; selections apply; onscreen keyboard does not obscure focused fields in a way that prevents interaction.

10) Accessibility check
- Steps: Use a screen reader and keyboard-only navigation to traverse all tests above.
- Expected: All controls announce their role and state; lists announce open/closed and selection changes.

Implementation notes

- Add unit/integration tests for the keyboard handlers of selection lists and dialog focus management.
- Add an end-to-end test (Cypress/Playwright) that automates the acceptance tests 1–4 and 8.
- Document the final tab order and keyboard shortcuts in the component README.

Related

- discovered-from:WL-000 (if there is an existing work item referencing Update window navigation)

data.description:
Problem statement
-----------------
`wl init` currently copies the global `AGENTS.md` into new projects (or appends it) which duplicates guidance and can create contradictory or stale local rules. We need `wl init` to prefer a single canonical global `AGENTS.md` while allowing a project's local `AGENTS.md` to declare project-specific overrides via a short pointer line.

Users
-----
- Project maintainers who want a single source of truth for agent guidance and the ability to declare small local exceptions.
- Agent authors and automation that rely on `AGENTS.md` to behave consistently across repositories.

Example user stories
- As a project maintainer, when I run `wl init` I want the project to reference the global `AGENTS.md` and allow me to add local exceptions so I avoid duplicated guidance.
- As an automation author, I want `wl init` behaviour to be idempotent so repeated runs do not create duplicate pointer lines or duplicate content.

Success criteria
----------------
- The local `AGENTS.md` begins with this exact pointer line (or preserves an existing exact match):
  "Follow the global AGENTS.md in addition to the rules below. The local rules below take priority in the event of a conflict."
- If a local `AGENTS.md` already exists, `wl init` prompts the operator before modifying it (non-destructive by default); if approved, the pointer is inserted near the top and the existing content is preserved unchanged except for trimming trailing whitespace.
- Running `wl init` multiple times is a no-op with respect to `AGENTS.md` (idempotent): no duplicate pointer lines, no duplicated global content.
- Unit and integration tests validate pointer insertion and idempotence on POSIX shells (Linux/macOS) and a minimal integration test demonstrates `wl init` behavior in CI.
- Documentation and release notes updated to describe the pointer requirement and the interactive behaviour for existing files.

Constraints
-----------
- Pointer text must match the exact line above for acceptance criteria (projects may have equivalent wording but the implementation will look for the exact pointer string to guarantee idempotence).
- Tests are focused on POSIX shell environments (Linux/macOS); Windows behaviour is out of scope for this change.
- For repositories with an existing `AGENTS.md`, `wl init` must not modify files without operator approval (interactive prompt or documented non-interactive flag to skip changes).
- Changes must be idempotent and safe for automated CI runs (non-destructive by default).

Existing state
--------------
- Repository root contains a global `AGENTS.md` with the agent workflow and WL conventions.
- Current `wl init` behaviour copies global `AGENTS.md` content into projects or appends content, causing duplicated guidance (described in work item SA-0MLCUNY9M0QN37A7). Several repository files and skills mention `AGENTS.md` and depend on consistent agent guidance.

Desired change
--------------
- Update `wl init`/template generation logic to:
  1. Detect whether a local `AGENTS.md` exists.
  2. If none exists, create `AGENTS.md` that begins with the exact pointer line and then (optionally) append any minimal project-specific starter rules.
  3. If a local `AGENTS.md` exists, do not modify it silently: prompt the operator during `wl init` (non-interactive runs may skip or record a suggested change) and, if approved, insert the exact pointer at the top and preserve the remainder of the file.
  4. Ensure the insertion logic is idempotent (no duplicate pointers on re-run).

Related work
------------
- Potentially related docs:
  - `AGENTS.md` — canonical global guidance used by `wl init` (`AGENTS.md`).
  - `skill/create-worktree-skill/README.md` — notes about `wl init` usage in CI and worktree setup (`skill/create-worktree-skill/README.md`).
  - `skill/create-worktree-skill/SKILL.md` and `scripts/run.sh` — places where non-interactive `wl init` is invoked and where insertion behavior matters (`skill/create-worktree-skill/SKILL.md`, `skill/create-worktree-skill/scripts/run.sh`).

- Potentially related work items:
  - `wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md and make local workflow rules override` — SA-0MLCUNY9M0QN37A7 (this item).
  - `Orchestration` — SA-0MKXVC7NA0UQLDR7 — broader agent workflow conventions that rely on `AGENTS.md`.
  - `Swarmable Plans` — SA-0MKXVTHF70EXG01D — references `AGENTS.md` for agent workflow guidance in planning contexts.
  - `Create worktree and branch` skill items — SA-0ML0502B21WHXDYA / SA-0ML05054Q0S4KAUD — integration tests and CI harnesses that run `wl init` and assume consistent `AGENTS.md` behaviour.
data.title: wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer

Summary

Replace brittle practice of recording audits inside comments with a structured per-item audit field. The audit field stores the time of the audit and the text of the audit. When a new audit is recorded it overwrites the existing audit for that work item.

User story

As a developer/maintainer, I want audits stored as a structured field on a work item (not buried in comments) so that tooling can reliably read/write audits, and audit metadata (time + text) is strongly typed and easily searchable.

Expected behaviour

- wl update <id> --audit "<ISO8601-timestamp> | <text>" (or equivalent --audit-time and --audit-text args) adds or replaces the audit field on the specified work item.
- The audit field contains: time (ISO8601 string) and text (string).
- When --audit is provided the existing audit is overwritten.
- wl show <id> includes the audit field in its output (JSON and human-readable formats).

Acceptance criteria

1. A new work-item field named audit (or clearly documented equivalent) exists and stores { "time": "...", "text": "..." }.
2. wl update <id> --audit "<timestamp>|<text>" updates the work item and overwrites any previous audit.
3. wl show <id> --json and default wl show display the audit field.
4. Unit tests cover parsing/validation and overwrite behaviour.
5. CLI help (wl update --help) documents the new flag and expected format.

Implementation notes / suggestions

- Prefer two flags --audit-time <ISO8601> and --audit-text "..." for clarity, or accept a single --audit "<timestamp>|<text>" string and parse it.
- Validate the timestamp (ISO8601); if invalid, return an error.
- Store audit as structured metadata on the work item (not in comments). Update persistence layer and API/DB model accordingly.
- Provide a small migration CLI or script (optional) to transform legacy comment-based audits into the new field for important items.
- Add unit/integration tests and update CLI docs.

Notes / risks

- This change is backward compatible for read-only clients; existing comment-based audits remain in history but new audits will be stored in the structured field.
- Consider whether audit history is needed; current requirement is to overwrite existing audit when a new one is recorded.
data.title: Replace comment-based audits with structured audit field

Summary:
Using the internal opencode interface (`o`) to create a work item results in the item being created in the Sorra Agents repository located under the user's config directory (~/.config/opencode / "Sorra Agents").

Impact:
- Work items intended for this repository are leaked into the user's global opencode configuration repository (Sorra Agents).
- Causes data leakage, confusion, and potential permission/ownership issues.
- High risk for privacy and integrity; affects all users running the internal `o` tool.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Run the internal opencode interface `o` and create a new work item (e.g. `o create "Test bug" --description "..."`).
2. Observe that the created work item appears in the Sorra Agents repo under `~/.config/opencode` instead of the target repository's worklog.

Expected behaviour:
- Work items created via `o` should be created in the active project repository's worklog, not in the global `~/.config/opencode` directory.

Suggested root causes to investigate:
- Hardcoded path or environment variable pointing to `~/.config/opencode` when resolving the wl data store.
- Incorrect handling of relative vs absolute paths when invoked from the internal interface.
- Use of a global configuration store without respecting the current project's working directory or repository context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fix implemented so `o` creates work items in the active repository's worklog by default.
- Add tests that verify work item creation context for `o` in both project and global contexts.
- Update documentation to clarify where `o` stores work items and how the context is determined.
- No user data is written to `~/.config/opencode` unless explicitly requested.

Notes:
- Create any follow-up tasks for code audit, tests, and a patch to correct path resolution.
data.title: Critical: opencode 'o' creates work items in Sorra Agents (~/.config/opencode)

Summary

Pressing the Escape (ESC) key causes the application to exit entirely. ESC should not terminate the program; at most it should close a modal, cancel an in-progress action, or be ignored when no cancellable UI is open.

User stories

- As a user, I want pressing ESC to cancel or close the current dialog instead of quitting the app so I don't lose work unexpectedly.
- As a user, I expect explicit quit actions (menu > Quit, Ctrl+C in terminal, or a dedicated shortcut) to be required to terminate the program.

Expected behaviour

- Pressing ESC will close the topmost transient UI element (modal, dropdown, inline editor) or do nothing if there is no such element.
- Pressing ESC must not cause the application process to exit.

Steps to reproduce

1. Start the application.
2. Ensure there is no explicit quit confirmation shown.
3. Press the ESC key.
4. Observe that the application exits (current behaviour).

Suggested implementation

- Add a global key handler that intercepts ESC key events and routes them to UI components/menus rather than allowing process-level exit.
- Ensure terminal-level handlers (if any) do not translate ESC into SIGINT or process termination.
- Add unit/integration tests covering key handling and a manual QA checklist for desktop and terminal environments.

Acceptance criteria

1. Reproduction: before the fix, ESC exits the app on the reported platform(s).
2. After the fix, pressing ESC does not terminate the process in any tested environment.
3. Pressing ESC closes modals or cancels in-progress operations when appropriate.
4. Automated tests for ESC handling are added and pass in CI.
5. A comment or short note is added to the relevant input/key handling code explaining the change.

Notes / Implementation hints

- If the app uses a UI framework that already maps ESC to window close, override that mapping only in places where the behaviour is undesirable.
- Investigate whether terminal/TTY libraries (if applicable) are translating ESC sequences into control sequences that lead to exit.
- Add `discovered-from: none` in description if creating additional follow-ups is necessary.
data.title: ESC should not exit the program

data.description:
Summary:
Under certain circumstances the update dialog's keyboard handling registers every keypress three times (e.g. typing 'a' results in 'aaa'). This is reproducible and breaks text input in the dialog.

Why it's critical:
- Blocks users from reliably entering text into the update dialog
- Can cause data corruption or repeated commands

Reproduction steps:
1. Open the application and navigate to the Update dialog (Settings → Update).
2. Click into the text input field (or focus it via keyboard).
3. Perform the steps that trigger the bug: observed when the dialog is opened while a background input listener is active — preconditions: open Update dialog while global keyboard shortcut handler is enabled and the devtools console shows no errors.
4. Type any character; each keypress is inserted three times.

Observed behavior:
- Each single keypress is registered and inserted three times into the input field.

Expected behavior:
- Each keypress should be registered once.

Suggested root causes to investigate:
- Duplicate event listeners attached to the input or window (listener attached on each dialog open without removal).
- Global keyboard shortcut handler forwarding events to the dialog as well as the input.
- Race condition causing event handler to be bound multiple times.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fix prevents triple key registration for all input fields in the Update dialog under all app states where it previously occurred.
- Add unit or integration tests to cover single keypress behavior in the dialog.
- Add a small manual test checklist in the issue to verify behavior across platforms (Linux/macOS/Windows if supported).
- Add a short note to the changelog or release notes if behaviour change is user visible.

Suggested implementation approach:
1. Audit the update dialog lifecycle to find where keydown/keypress/keyup listeners are registered and ensure they are only added once and removed on dialog close.
2. Prefer attaching listeners to the input element rather than the global window if appropriate.
3. If global listeners must remain, guard handlers with a check to ignore events originated from input elements or ensure event.stopPropagation/stopImmediatePropagation is used properly.
4. Add automated tests that mount the dialog, simulate a single key event, and assert a single insertion.

Manual verification checklist:
- Open Update dialog, focus input, type text -> each key appears once.
- Reopen dialog multiple times -> typing still registers single keypress.
- Toggle global shortcuts on/off and verify behavior.

References and context:
- Observed during QA session 2026-02-08; no existing work item found in repo referencing this exact failure.

Origin: accidentally submitted to another project as SA-0MLDICHPG1GR6J8G.
data.title: Update dialog keyboard registers triple keypresses

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
Fixed textarea viewport/scrolling issue when using Ctrl+Enter

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add a new line, the first line would disappear and only reappear when typing a character.

Root cause: The textarea was setting the new value before the dialog had expanded, causing rendering issues with the viewport.

Solution in commit cdf5991:
- Update layout and expand dialog BEFORE setting the new value
- Improved scroll calculation to properly keep cursor line visible
- Added viewport handling when box height changes
- Force internal cursor update to refresh the display

The textarea now properly displays all content when adding new lines.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
FOUND THE ROOT CAUSE! Fixed textarea scroll issue in commit abe7e24

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add lines, the first line would disappear.

Root Cause: The textarea has scrollable=true and maintains internal scroll state. When adding a newline:
1. The cursor moves to line 2
2. The dialog expands to fit 2 lines
3. But the textarea's scroll position wasn't being reset
4. If scroll was > 0, line 1 would be scrolled off the top

Solution: Explicitly set scroll to 0 whenever totalLines <= visibleLines. This ensures all content is visible from the top when it fits in the viewport.

The fix was simple - we were only setting scroll when content EXCEEDED the visible area, but never resetting it to 0 when content should be fully visible.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
SUCCESS! Fixed the Ctrl+Enter textarea rendering issue in commit ae5b9e2

The root cause was finally identified:
1. Ctrl+Enter sends a 'linefeed' keypress event (not 'C-enter')
2. Blessed's textarea handles this internally and inserts the newline
3. Our .key(['C-enter']) handler never ran because blessed processed it first
4. We were resizing AFTER the newline was inserted, causing scroll issues

The solution:
- Intercept the 'linefeed' keypress event BEFORE blessed processes it
- Read the current line count
- Calculate the future line count (current + 1)
- Resize the dialog preemptively to the correct height
- Let blessed insert the newline naturally
- Scroll to bottom after insertion completes

Now when pressing Ctrl+Enter:
- The box expands smoothly
- All content remains visible
- The cursor stays visible on the new line
- No content scrolls off screen unexpectedly

This was a complex debugging journey that involved understanding blessed's internal event handling!

Audit: Enumerated all event listener usages (\.on/\.once) under src/ and noted recommended cleanup actions. Summary:

- Files requiring explicit cleanup (transient UI widgets, child processes, SSE): src/tui/opencode-client.ts, src/commands/tui.ts, src/tui/components/modals.ts, src/tui/components/dialogs.ts, src/tui/components/opencode-pane.ts, src/tui/components/overlays.ts, src/tui/components/list.ts, src/tui/components/detail.ts, src/tui/components/help-menu.ts, src/tui/components/toast.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-navigation.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-submit.ts

- Recommendations (per-file):
  * Remove/deregister listeners on destroy for transient blessed widgets (use removeAllListeners or remove specific handlers) — applicable to all files creating widgets: components/* and commands/tui.ts.
  * Child process handlers (stdout/stderr/error/close) should be registered once and removed in stop/cleanup; ensure proc.kill() is preceded by removing listeners and nulling refs.
  * SSE/HTTP request listeners must be removed/aborted on stream finish/error to avoid late payload processing (opencode-client.ts).
  * Add unit tests that create/destroy widgets and start/stop child processes repeatedly to assert listener counts do not grow and no duplicate handling occurs.

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment:
Plan to fix overwrite (single-machine, concurrent writers):

Root cause: multiple WorklogDatabase instances hold stale snapshots. Any write exports the instance snapshot to JSONL, so a stale instance can overwrite newer changes from another instance.

Recommended fix (Option 1): merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
- Before writing JSONL, load current JSONL from disk and merge with in-memory snapshot using mergeWorkItems/mergeComments (newer updatedAt wins; non-default beats default).
- Write merged result back to JSONL.
Why it works: prevents stale writers from overwriting newer fields; each write reconciles with latest on-disk state.

Alternatives:
- Import-before-write guard based on JSONL mtime (simpler but still racey).
- File lock around JSONL writes (robust but more complexity).

Plan:
1) Implement merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
2) Update failing regression test in tests/sync.test.ts to pass.
3) Run npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts.

Expected outcome: stale snapshot imports no longer revert recent updates.

data.comment: Fixed in commit 1f9d695. Root cause: editTextarea used blessed.list for buttons, which does not reliably emit select on mouse clicks, causing the modal Promise to never resolve. Replaced with blessed.box widgets (same pattern as confirmTextbox). Also simplified resetInputState by removing aggressive workarounds. All 327 tests pass, build clean.

data.author: @opencode
data.comment: Second fix in commit 76e2f17. Found the deeper root cause: blessed textarea with inputOnFocus=true sets screen.grabKeys=true when readInput() is called on focus. This blocks ALL screen-level key handlers. The previous fix (replacing blessed.list buttons with blessed.box) was necessary but not sufficient -- the textarea's readInput cycle was never properly ended during cleanup, leaving grabKeys permanently true. Now cleanup explicitly calls textarea.cancel() to end the readInput cycle before destroying widgets, plus grabKeys=false safety nets in all cleanup paths including forceCleanup().

data.author: opencode
data.comment:
Findings: 
- next filtering excludes status='deleted' in WorklogDatabase.findNextWorkItemFromItems, so a truly deleted item should not be selected.
- CLI delete (src/commands/delete.ts) calls db.delete which removes the row from SQLite (not soft-delete). TUI 'delete' uses db.update status='deleted'.
- WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl merges DB items with disk JSONL (src/database.ts). If an item was deleted from DB, but still exists in disk JSONL, mergeWorkItems will keep the JSONL item (it is treated as a real item, not a tombstone).
- refreshFromJsonlIfNewer re-imports JSONL back into DB when JSONL mtime is newer. This can resurrect deleted items (the DB delete isn't represented as a deletion in JSONL), and then wl next can surface it.
Hypothesis: deletion via CLI (hard delete) + stale JSONL + refresh/merge can resurrect the item, causing wl next to return it. Fix likely needs a tombstone or deletion record in JSONL or merge logic to drop items absent from DB when DB has newer state (or set status='deleted' instead of hard delete).
